sites.name: Le Monde EN
sites.note: Le Monde's English path exposes the configurable gdpr-lmd CMP. Reject should use only the explicit denyAll action. The French root path can instead show a consent-or-pay wall and should be treated as an honest site-specific choice for reject/custom.

sites.name: Le Monde Root (Accept Override)
sites.note: French root consent-or-pay wall with the user's site-specific Always Accept override. This should accept the wall directly and must not run the /en/ post-accept settings recovery, which can open Le Monde's withdrawal modal.

sites.name: Le Monde (Accept)
sites.note: Accept All with CCPA do-not-sell enabled must save via Le Monde settings so analytics/personalization/social/media-platform purposes are on while ads stay off.

sites.name: Le Monde (Accept No CCPA)
sites.note: Accept All with CCPA do-not-sell disabled must save via Le Monde settings so every configurable purpose remains enabled when cookie preferences are reopened.

sites.name: Le Monde (Custom Functional)
sites.note: Custom must open settings and save Le Monde purpose toggles on the English gdpr-lmd CMP, not fall through to denyAll. Functional maps to personalization; analytics, social, media-platform, and ads remain off. User-opened footer cookie settings must remain inspectable and not be auto-saved.

sites.name: Der Spiegel
sites.note: As of August 8, 2026 the first-layer banner is a consent-or-pay wall (Consent and continue / Subscribe now / Preferences, sp_choice_type_11/9/12) with no direct Reject All (no sp_choice_type_REJECT_ALL, no data-sp-action=REJECT_ALL). Reject requires opening Preferences, which loads a separate privacy-manager frame using per-category Accept/Reject button pairs instead of a bulk reject-all control (sp-frame-handler.js's rejectFromPrivacyManager() now handles this via rejectAllPrivacyManagerCategories()). The full open-frame-load-reject-save sequence needs more time than the default handleWaitMs.

sites.name: DW Accept All
sites.note: US/no-VPN direct top-stories accept path. If DW detours into the full privacy-settings page, Accept All must save the settings surface and return to content rather than strand the user on Save selection.

sites.name: DW Custom
sites.note: US/no-VPN direct top-stories path. Custom must click DW's plain first-layer Settings link, apply preferences in the ConsentManager settings surface, save, and leave the banner gone.

sites.name: DW
sites.note: DW sometimes redirects into a full-page privacy manager; validate both the entry banner and settings page paths.

sites.name: The Verge
sites.note: Live fingerprint probe on July 19, 2026 found OneTrust SDK assets plus Launchpad / LiveRamp privacy scripts on the public homepage. The non-VPN validation run handled the current surface via dom:onetrust:ccpa rather than the older Sourcepoint path.

sites.name: FIFA
sites.note: US/no-VPN public homepage shows a top-level OneTrust shell with visible Reject All / I'm OK with that / Preference Center controls while the full category preference center sits hidden in the DOM. Custom mode must open the preference center, keep Functional on, turn Performance and Targeting off, save, and dismiss the visible shell.

sites.name: FIFA (Reject All)
sites.note: US/no-VPN reject-all should persist the privacy-center state and record activity, not just leave the hidden OneTrust categories flipped without counting the action.

sites.name: Thomson Reuters Homepage
sites.note: Homepage exposes a visible OneTrust shell with only a Cookie Settings opener. The working path is: open the privacy center, apply RejectAll via OneTrust's API, confirm choices, and let cleanup remove the visible shell.

sites.name: KPMG OneTrust Article
sites.note: KPMG's OneTrust PC2 center exposes both Submit All Preferences and Agree & Proceed. Custom mode must click the preference submit control, not the accept/proceed control, then dismiss without reopening or leaving the page scrolled to the footer.

sites.name: People
sites.note: US flow uses a OneTrust shell with Cookie Settings / Accept All and a privacy center that has recently exposed a single targeting-style opt-out toggle in headed manual checks. Automation often sees the shell hidden in DOM, so activity recording is the primary signal here.

sites.name: Investopedia
sites.note: People Inc. OneTrust US flow mirrors people.com: reject-all must persist the privacy-choice opt-out in the OneTrust preference center, not just dismiss the shell.

sites.name: La Repubblica
sites.note: Current wall exposes accept or subscribe paths; the non-accept continuation control is rendered hidden in validation.

sites.name: ABC España
sites.note: Evolok paywall. Reject requires paid subscription (€3.99+/month). Accept is the only free path. Extension handles accept_all only.

sites.name: La Vanguardia
sites.note: Evolok paywall. Reject requires paid subscription. Accept is the only free path. Extension handles accept_all only.

sites.name: Corriere della Sera
sites.note: Current wall exposes accept or subscribe paths; no free reject path was confirmed during validation.

sites.name: Il Sole 24 Ore
sites.note: Current wall presents subscription-oriented alternatives; a reliable free reject flow was not confirmed in validation.

sites.name: La Stampa
sites.note: Current wall exposes accept or subscribe-oriented paths; no reliable free reject action was confirmed in validation.

sites.name: Il Messaggero
sites.note: Current wall exposes accept or subscribe-oriented paths; no reliable free reject action was confirmed in validation.

sites.name: Público
sites.note: Portuguese locale coverage target. Human validation is still needed to confirm the active CMP and whether a reliable free reject path exists.

sites.name: Harrods
sites.note: Didomi detected by script fingerprint but banner not found in e2e — may use a delayed or iframe-based Didomi variant. Requires --vpn to load (bot-protected). Needs human validation to confirm banner selectors.

sites.name: Inchcape
sites.note: Investis Digital Cookie Manager v3.1. The live EU shell uses #__cookieWrapper with direct Accept/Decline buttons and a modal preference center. Custom mode should map Functional=true, Performance=false, Marketing=false, then save and dismiss the wrapper.

sites.name: Allround Automations
sites.note: US traffic currently gets Cookiebot by Usercentrics with a level-selection dialog. The API records consent, but the banner needs an explicit Cookiebot.hide() after submitCustomConsent()/withdraw() to disappear.

sites.name: LVMH
sites.note: No reject-all button — GDPR toggle-style banner with Functional/Targeting/Performance groups. Needs manage-preferences path. Requires --vpn to load (bot-protected).

sites.name: ANTA EU (VPN Custom)
sites.note: ANTA's cookie policy identifies the storefront as Shopify-hosted, so this target is intended to validate the generic Shopify Customer Privacy path from an EU/VPN session.

sites.name: CLUSE EU (VPN Custom)
sites.note: CLUSE is Shopify-hosted but the live EU consent surface is Pandectes, not Shopify Customer Privacy, so this target validates the Pandectes flow instead.

sites.name: Bare Biology EU (VPN Custom)
sites.note: Bare Biology is Shopify-hosted but the live EU consent surface is Consentmo in a shadow-root custom element, so this target validates the Consentmo flow instead.

sites.name: Renais EU (VPN Custom)
sites.note: Renais's cookie policy documents Shopify privacy cookies including _tracking_consent and _cmp_a, so this target is intended to validate the generic Shopify Customer Privacy path from an EU/VPN session.

sites.name: e-Core (HubSpot Cookie Banner)
sites.note: Live fingerprint probe on July 19, 2026 saw AdOpt DOM (`#cookie-banner`) and `tag.goadopt.io` scripts on top of HubSpot assets. The visible reject path in the non-VPN run recorded via dom:privacymanager:reject_all rather than a HubSpot-specific method.

sites.name: Canadian Tire (US/OneTrust/Custom)
sites.note: From US (no VPN), Canadian Tire shows the full OneTrust PC2 preference center directly instead of the simple accept/reject banner shown to CA visitors. Custom mode must keep Functional on, dismiss the visible PC, preserve the hidden OneTrust scaffold, restore scroll after handling, and keep the footer Cookie Settings reopen view synchronized with the saved group state.

sites.name: Canadian Tire (EU/OneTrust/Reject)
sites.note: From EU (VPN), Canadian Tire shows the full OneTrust PC2 preference center. Reject mode uses OneTrust.RejectAll(), then closes the visible PC without deleting the reusable preference-center DOM so footer Cookie Settings still works afterward.
